title: FairPriceEstimate
description: ML fair-price estimate plus the deterministic, capped deal_score computed in Python from stated weighted components (architecture.md §10.3). The price-advantage contribution is capped so one erroneous prediction cannot dominate ranking. schema_version 1.1.0 (Checkpoint C.0, docs/adr/0003-phase2-checkpoint-c0-serving-contract.md §3) resolves a structural conflict: itinerary_accessibility is System-B-owned and caller-supplied, so Travel-MCP-only serving cannot always produce it. deal_score/components are now conditionally required on scoring_status, never fabricated or silently redistributed when incomplete. Every existing 1.0.0 instance (unconditionally complete) remains valid unchanged.

interval.description: Split-conformal calibrated interval (phase2/ml/calibration.py) -- a statistical coverage statement about the model on historical data, never a guarantee about a real future price.

lower_minor_units.description: Serving-response value: clamped to 0 if the raw calibrated lower bound was negative. See lower_bound_clamped. This is a serving representation rule, never a change to the trained artifact, the calibration quantile, or its target_coverage.

lower_bound_clamped.description: True iff the raw split-conformal lower bound (prediction - quantile) was negative and was clamped to 0 for this response.

scoring_status.description: 'incomplete' when a required deal_score component (typically itinerary_accessibility, which is System-B-owned) is not available. Never redistribute the missing weight or fabricate a neutral value -- see missing_components/incomplete_reason.

allOf.description: 1.0.0: exactly the original contract (deal_score/components always required), PLUS Checkpoint C.0.1: explicitly forbid every 1.1-only state field individually, so a 1.0.0 payload can never claim 'incomplete' or otherwise become contradictory.
1.1.0 complete: deal_score/components required; incomplete-only fields forbidden INDIVIDUALLY (not just as a pair), so a payload cannot bypass the gate by supplying only one of them.
1.1.0 incomplete: missing_components/incomplete_reason required; deal_score/components forbidden INDIVIDUALLY (not just as a pair), so a payload cannot bypass the gate by supplying only one of them.
